LogoParamountPlus More live games and exclusives Log Out Connect TV Provider More live games & exclusives Log Out Connect NFL News & Highlights Sole possession of first place in the NFC North is on the line at Ford Field as two 8-2 rivals clash on Thanksgiving with long winning streaks Imagn Images In the first of three Thanksgiving day games, the Detroit Lions play host to the division rival Chicago Bears in one of the biggest games of the NFL season to date. Detroit enters this game winners of six straight and sitting in first place in the NFC North with an 8-2 record. The Lions sport one of the NFL's most efficient and explosive offenses, and their efense hasn't allowed more than 21 points in a game since all the way back in Week 4. The Lions are dealing with injury issues on that side of the ball, but they've held up surprisingly well. That will be put to the test on Thursday afternoon. Chicago comes into this game having won five in a row and sporting an 8-2 record that matches that of Detroit, with the Bears sitting in second place in the division by virtue of a tiebreaker. The Bears also have one of the league's best offenses, while the defense has been strengthened by the acquisition of superstar defensive lineman Jeffery Simmons , who seems to have transformed the unit up front and allowed everything else to click properly into place. That unit, too, will be tested more than ever here. Which of these two teams will keep its winning streak alive and lay claim to sole possession of first place in the division? We'll find out soon enough. Before we break down the matchup, here's a look at how you can watch the game. Where to watch Lions vs. Bears live Date: Thursday, Nov. 26 | Time: 1 p.m. ET Location: Ford Field (Detroit) TV: CBS | Streaming: Paramount+ Follow: CBS Sports App Odds: Bears -2.5, O/U 55.5 via DraftKings Sportsbook When the Bears have the ball Chicago is eighth in total yards and eighth in total points this season, but some of that has to do with volume. The Bears rank a surprising 14th in yards per play, 12th in points per drive and 15th in EPA per play, according to Tru Media. Some of that is due to the fact that Caleb Williams missed several games with a hamstring injury, but even with Williams on the field the Bears' EPA per play mark is only the equivalent of the 10th-best offense in the league. Chicago is one of the league's most run-oriented offenses, ranking ninth in the share of plays that turn into a rush attempt. But D'Andre Swift is averaging just 3.7 yards per carry and Kyle Monangai , who has been more effective (5.0 per carry) has played in only five games. The Lions have sported a top run defense this season in allowing only 4.0 yards per carry, but that defense took a couple of massive hits over the last few weeks with the losses of Jack Campbell and Aidan Hutchinson to injury. Still, Detroit held Tampa Bay's running backs to 84 yards on 22 carries last Sunday, when Bucky Irving and Kenneth Gainwell had previously been destroying teams on the ground. The Bears will need Swift and Monangai to find more success if they want to control the game in the fashion they have preferred since Ben Johnson became head coach last year. Chicago's passing game has been relatively inconsistent this year, as there have been times when Caleb Williams has looked like an elite quarterback and others when he has looked ordinary — sometimes within the same game. (Like the Sunday night showdown against the Buccaneers , for example.) Williams has completed 68.3% of his passes at 7.9 yards per attempt, but he's thrown only 10 touchdown passes against six interceptions. He's 11th in the NFL in EPA per dropback, according to Tru Media, but he's been highly susceptible against the blitz: he ranks fourth in EPA against four-man rushes but only checks in 19th when opponents rush five or more. Detroit has blitzed at a below-average rate this season (30.3%, per Tru Media), but would be wise to turn up the pressure a bit against a quarterback who has shown that he can be pressured into some bad decisions on occasion if you get defenders into his lap. Still, the Lions have been highly susceptible to opposing passing attacks, even if they have been improved since the return of Brian Branch and should get another lift as Kerby Joseph rounds into form. The Lions are 27th in EPA per dropback allowed, and they're in the bottom third in opponents' explosive play rate through the air. Detroit is most vulnerable against opposing tight ends, allowing the league's fifth-highest target share to the position, so this could be a game where the Bears finally get Colston Loveland going in a way that they haven't been able to accomplish as much as they likely wanted to this year. The Lions do limit yards after the catch better than any defense in the NFL, though, allowing only 4.0 YAC per completion, according to Tru Media. That could take away from some of Chicago's success in the screen game and possibly limit the effectiveness of Luther Burden III and — to a lesser extent because he's not as big a part of the offense — Kalif Raymond . When the Lions have the ball The Lions are third in the NFL in yards and fifth in points. They're fifth in both yards per play and points per drive, as well as fifth in EPA per play, according to Tru Media. They're second in EPA per pass attempt and third in EPA per rush attempt. They're third in passing success rate, first in rushing success rate and third in overall success rate. They are, in other words, a top-five offense by almost any measurement, and they can beat you with both the pass and the run. Jared Goff is having a marvelous season, completing 67.8% of his passes at an average of 8.2 yards per attempt with 20 touchdown passes against six interceptions. He's third in the league behind only Brock Purdy and Joe Burrow in EPA per dropback, third behind only Purdy and Burrow in success rate and fourth behind only Purdy, Burrow and Patrick Mahomes in passer rating. His 8.2 yards-per-attempt average is the second-best of his tenure in Detroit, as are the 52.3% success rate and 107.7 passer rating. He's of course blessed with one of the best skill-position corps in the league: Amon-Ra St. Brown is a picture of consistency; Jameson Williams is one of the most explosive threats in football; Sam LaPorta is a strong option and tight end; and Jahmyr Gibbs is the best running back in the NFL, leading the league in rushes, rushing yards, first downs, yards from scrimmage and total touchdowns. St. Brown often gets pigeonholed as a slot guy, but in reality he plays more outside (59.2% of snaps) than he does inside (39.8%), according to Tru Media, and he's equally capable of dominating defenses from either spot. He's Goff's first read more often than not because he runs a lot of short-area routes and the Lions like to get the ball out fairly quickly in their straight dropback game, where St. Brown is often the target. Williams is the guy the Lions turn toward when they're looking to test defenses in the intermediate and deep areas of the field. His 12.36-yard average route depth is fourth among 199 players who have run 100 or more routes this season, according to Tru Media, and he's generated an explosive gain (16-plus yards) on 26.3% of his targets, which ranks 17th among that same group of players. He and LaPorta are generally going to eat into each other's target shares in any given week, while St. Brown remains the more consistent top target. The Bears' secondary is beatable, as Chicago ranks 22nd in net yards allowed per attempt, according to Pro-Football-Reference. Jaylon Johnson is not the same player he once was, Tyrique Stevenson is inconsistent, Kyler Gordon has barely played and Malik Muhammad has the ups and downs of a fourth-round rookie. If the Lions give Goff time to throw, he could feast on this group all afternoon. That's where Chicago's improved defensive line comes in. Since acquiring Jeffery Simmons, the Bears rank seventh in the league in EPA per dropback, per Tru Media, in large part because they have recorded a sack on 10.7% of opponent dropbacks. Prior to acquiring Simmons, Chicago's sack rate was 8.9%. That figure still ranked third in the league through seven weeks, but it's been much improved since the Bears dropped Simmons into the middle of the defensive line. Detroit is pretty strong up front, allowing pressure on only 32.3% of dropbacks, which ranks sixth in the NFL. The sack rate is a bit worse than that because Goff isn't the world's most mobile quarterback, but he's generally given adequate time to throw. LogoParamountPlus More live games and exclusives Log Out Connect TV Provider More live games & exclusives Log Out Connect NFL News & Highlights CBS Sports writers Jordan Dajani and Jared Dubin predict this weekend's top games Getty Images Welcome to the most special week in the NFL . We watched the Los Angeles Rams defeat the Green Bay Packers on Wednesday night, and now, we have three exciting Thanksgiving matchups to digest this "Turkey Day." Football fans suffered through many sleepy Chicago Bears vs. Detroit Lions Thanksgiving matchups over the years. Now, this 1 p.m. game on Thursday is expected to be one of the most exciting holiday matchups in recent memory. After that, the Dallas Cowboys will welcome Joe Milton III and the Philadelphia Eagles to AT&T Stadium. Both teams are coming off wins, and the Cowboys need this game if they want to keep pace in the NFC East. At the end of the night, we have a potential AFC Championship preview to watch when the Buffalo Bills host Patrick Mahomes and the Kansas City Chiefs . This is just the second game in NFL history to feature two teams coming off at least three straight 17-point victories. Which teams should you pick in Week 12, and which should you fade? CBS Sports writers Jordan Dajani and Jared Dubin are here to break down the biggest games of the weekend. For clarity, lines for these selections were taken on Nov. 25 over at DraftKings Sportsbook. Credit to CBS Sports Research Chicago Bears (-1.5) at Detroit Lions (Thursday) Dajani (Bears -1.5): I can't remember being more excited for a Thanksgiving Day game, as the Bears and Lions are two of the best teams in the NFL. What I keep going back to is that the Bears are 6-0 while averaging 33.7 points in games where Caleb Williams starts and finishes. Then, factor in how much improved this Chicago defense looks with the addition of Jeffery Simmons . In Weeks 1-7, they ranked dead last in both yards per play (6.3) and yards per attempt (8.7). Over the last four weeks, the Bears now rank in the top 10 in both categories. Chicago has been swept by Detroit in each of the last two seasons. I think the Bears are done with losing to Dan Campbell … Prediction: Bears 30, Lions 28 Dubin (Lions +1.5): These are two incredibly evenly-matched teams, but it seems like Detroit has more matchup advantages offensively against Chicago's improved defense than the Bears do against the Lions' own improved unit. With Detroit also getting the benefit of home-field advantage, we're rolling with the Lions to win a close one as a home underdog. … Prediction: Lions 31, Bears 30 Philadelphia Eagles at Dallas Cowboys (-8.5) (Thursday) Dajani (Cowboys -8.5): I don't think the Cowboys have exorcised all of their defensive demons just because they blew out the Tennessee Titans , but that win at home was just what this team needed. This is one of those cases where I think the Cowboys just simply out-score their opponent. This is still a rivalry, but the Eagles are 2-8 against the spread this season, which ranks second-worst in the NFL behind the Los Angeles Chargers , and are 0-5 against the spread in their last five divisional matchups. The Cowboys should get this cover in the fourth quarter. They have scored NINETY-ONE (91) points over the past two games! That's the most in a two-game span since 1971… Prediction: Cowboys 33, Eagles 20 Dubin (Eagles +8.5): I know they just beat the Titans by 21, but I don't like laying this many points with the Cowboys. Their defense is still too suspect and they are still too prone to games where they don't perform up to expectations for me to be comfortable with an 8.5-point spread. So even while I think they'll dent the scoreboard at home on Thanksgiving afternoon, I can't bring myself to predict that this will be a blowout. … Prediction: Cowboys 30, Eagles 24 Kansas City Chiefs at Buffalo Bills (-3) (Thursday) Dajani (Chiefs +3): The craziest part about this rivalry is that the Bills have won the last five regular-season meetings, while the Chiefs have won the last four playoff meetings! You should also know that the weather is supposed to be terrible on Thursday night, so this could come down to which team runs the ball better. James Cook has recorded nine straight games with 75 rushing yards and a touchdown. He and Josh Allen are the second duo to ever account for double-digit rushing touchdowns each through the first 10 games of a season. Meanwhile, on the other side, Emmett Johnson has rushed for 206 yards with 108 receiving yards and three touchdowns over the last two games in place of the injured Kenneth Walker III . I almost think a three-point spread in this matchup is pretty high. That's going to lead me to take the points even though Bills over Chiefs has been an auto-bet in the regular season recently… Prediction: Chiefs 17, Bills 16 Dubin (Bills -3): I have basically the exact same analysis of this game as Dajani but come down on the opposite side of the bet because of the Bills' regular-season history against the Chiefs and the relative strength of their run game. I trust Josh Allen and James Cook to run the ball more than I do Emmett Johnson, even with how good Johnson has been over the last two weeks. Could Patrick Mahomes make this prediction look silly? Of course. But I think that'll prove more difficult in Thursday night's expected weather. … Prediction: Bills 21, Chiefs 17 Denver Broncos (-3.5) at Pittsburgh Steelers (Friday) Dajani ( Broncos -3.5): Aaron Rodgers lobbed a grenade into the Pittsburgh Steelers facility as he exited it this week. Going on national television and calling your coach a narcoleptic, unhealthy, lazy person who doesn't even know the franchise he works for is insane. So, this is a moment that will ultimately rally the locker room, or cause them to completely fall apart. Pick which side you'd like. The Steelers have also won and covered in six straight home games. This seems like an appropriate time for that streak to end … Prediction: Broncos 20, Steelers 13 Dubin (Broncos -3.5): After the disaster that hit the Steelers this week, I just can't see them keeping the game close against the Broncos. No, I don't think they'll get the backup quarterback bounce from Mason Rudolph . I don't trust the Broncos as far as Bo Nix or I can throw them, but given the state the Steelers' locker room has to be in right now, I think you have to roll with Denver to cover this one with relative ease. … Prediction: Broncos 24, Steelers 10 Baltimore Ravens at Houston Texans (-7) Dajani ( Ravens +7): I have the Houston Texans winning this game, but seven points seems a bit high. C.J. Stroud is playing some great football, but his production has been overshadowed by a defense that has fallen from No. 2 in points allowed per game in 2025, to 17th this year. The Texans are 1-8 against the spread in their last nine home games following an ATS win. I'll take Baltimore to keep it close… Prediction: Texans 24, Ravens 18 Dubin (Ravens +7): The Ravens have now lost six straight, but they've lost the two games in the Jacoby Brissett era by a combined five points despite turning the ball over six times in those contests. If they can just limit the giveaways, I think they might even be able to pull off an upset against a Houston team that hasn't exactly lit the world on fire this year. Either way, I think they can keep it close by throwing on a surprisingly vulnerable Texans pass defense. … Prediction: Texans 24, Ravens 20 Seattle Seahawks at San Francisco 49ers (-3) Dajani ( 49ers -3): Sam Darnold is expected to return this week, and he's accounted for 10 touchdowns compared to nine interceptions in seven starts this season. If you throw out the season opener that Drew Lock finished and won, Darnold is 2-4 as a starter this season. Believe it or not, San Francisco is 0-9 against the spread in its last nine home divisional games. With the number at a field goal, the 49ers have a good chance to end that streak this week. What they did to the Minnesota Vikings in Mexico City last Sunday night was shocking. The 49ers should be headlining everyone's NFL power rankings if they weren't already. Their 0.19 EPA per play is the best mark since the 2018 Chiefs, and they have the best offensive success rate (54.8%) by any team in a season since at least 2000 … Prediction: 49ers 24, Seahawks 20 Dubin (49ers -3): I reserve the right to flip this prediction to Seattle if Brock Purdy is out with his ankle injury, but if he's in, I just think that this San Francisco offense is a buzzsaw that can't really be stopped — even by the Dark Side defense. Remember, they dropped 32 points on Seattle the last time out. And they've scored 35 or more in each of their three games since returning from the bye. I don't think they can be stopped when everyone is healthy. … Prediction: 49ers 30, Seahawks 23 Las Vegas Raiders at Cleveland Browns (-4.5) (SNF) Dajani ( Raiders +4.5): Maybe part of me is rooting for Fernando Mendoza

More than a thousand dollars raised to help pay for a local rescue dog’s surgery was nowhere to be found for months. That is, until NBC 5 Responds stepped in. When you donate money, you expect it to go to the person or pet in need. But when a local rescue dog needed surgery, more than a thousand dollars raised to help pay for it was nowhere to be found. He’s got attitude, flare and a face we’ll call unforgettable. “He has no bottom jaw and no basically no top jaw,” said Colleen Collins, founder of The Perfect Pooches Adoption Agency. Meet Dobby, a special needs rescue Chihuahua, and one of roughly 600 dogs Collins has helped find homes for through her nonprofit. “You see that big hole in his nose. So, I have to I have to like to blend up his food,” said Collins. Collins’ dogs require a lot of care. But to her, it’s a calling. “I was adopted as a baby, so people say maybe there’s some correlation there,” said Collins. Collins says adoption fees coming in don’t come close to covering the medical expenses for many of the dogs in her care. So earlier this year, she launched a fundraiser through a company called Spring to pay for Dobby’s eye surgery. And thanks to Dobby’s distinct features, it was their most successful fundraiser to date, raising more than a thousand dollars. There was just one problem. “I still had received zero dollars and August comes and goes, September comes and goes. He needed surgery to get his eye removed, which the quote was like two thousand dollars and I really need this money,” said Collins. “All of a sudden I got a notification email that Amaze paid me in my PayPal,” said Collins. “These are legacy issues for sure. We’ve dropped the ball here,” said Joel Kutz, CEO of Amaze. Joel Krutz took over as the CEO of Amaze earlier this year. The company previously went by the name “Spring”. “We are dealing with all responses within 24 hours now. In terms of the new Amaze commerce we haven’t had any incidents at all of late payments,” said Krutz. Krutz says he’s sorry Collins had to go to this length to get a resolution. “I appreciate her raising this. I appreciate that we could resolve it,” said Krutz. Collins said she thinks “the exposure” from NBC 5 Responds “probably pushed it over the edge.” And it was just in time for Dobby. “His surgery was Friday and he’s doing really well and I’m happy to say that I’m feel good, like the surgery is gonna be covered with the amount of money that we got,” said Collins. If you’re looking for a third party to help you with a fundraiser, the FTC says you should research the company and look for any bad reviews or red flags. A search of “Amaze Software Inc” shows a trail of complaints with the Better Business Bureau dating back three years. The CEO says his team is working on these “legacy issues” and to resolve any outstanding complaints.

The only time the Cowboys have won back-to-back games under head coach Brian Schottenheimer came back in his first season in 2025 following their Week 10 bye. That was a stretch of three victories in a row against Las Vegas Raiders (33-16), the Eagles (24-21) and the Kansas City Chiefs (31-28) on Thanksgiving Day. After Dallas' 51-30 victory over the Tennessee Titans (1-9) on Sunday, Cowboys owner and general manager Jerry Jones has some hope that his squad can make a postseason push down the stretch. That's just days after Jones called his Cowboys "a bad team" in the wake of their 46-40 home loss against the San Francisco 49ers (9-1) in Week 10. "It gives me hope that we can do some of the things that we wanted to do," Jones said postgame on Sunday. "We needed this kind of thing. Any team does. We needed to feel it and get a little wind under our wings, so to speak." Quarterback Dak Prescott looks to continue his high-level play on Thanksgiving. If he replicated his Sunday performance against the Titans (325 yards passing and four touchdowns on 28-of-33 passing with a rushing touchdown), that would give Prescott 19 passing touchdowns on Thanksgiving, the record for the most Thanksgiving Day touchdowns in NFL history. Prescott's predecessor Tony Romo and Matthew Stafford currently share the record with 18 Turkey Day passing touchdowns each. "It's a blessing. It's something that, one of my favorite games of the year," Prescott said Tuesday. "And so, just being able to put that uniform on with the John Madden seal on it, understanding the whole world's watching and how many little kids are in the position that I once was: watching the game and then ready to go outside and play my own version of it. ... I don't take it for granted." However, there's one Cowboy who doesn't look forward to Thanksgiving: defensive tackle Quinnen Williams . The four-time Pro Bowler doesn't enjoy the holiday because it goes against his in-season training and diet regimen. Williams' go-to Thanksgiving side dish is macaroni, something that is hard to resist this time of year. "It's during the season. I'm trying to stay lean and trim, and it's a holiday right around when real football starts to come in," said Williams. "So I'm not a big fan of Thanksgiving." That's okay, because there will be plenty of fans ready to see Williams on the field, especially against starting Eagles quarterback and former Cowboy Joe Milton. Dallas acquired Milton in a trade with the New England Patriots in April 2025, and he worked as one of Prescott's backups until the Eagles signed him off the Cowboys' practice squad on Oct. 17. That's the same day Philadelphia placed Super Bowl MVP quarterback Jalen Hurts (blood clots) on injured reserve. "Haha, it's good to see him," said Cowboys wide receiver CeeDee Lamb . "I hope he don't go crazy." Let's dig into the matchup. He became the fourth player in NFL history with 300-plus passing yards and five-plus total touchdowns in consecutive games across Weeks 10 and 11, per CBS Sports Research. He joined Daunte Culpepper (2004), Tom Brady (2007) and Ben Roethlisberger (2014) in this exclusive club. After racking up 1,003 yards passing, 11 touchdowns and just a single interception over the last three weeks, Prescott now ranks second in the league in passing yards (3,049) and second in passing touchdowns (25). He also ranks eighth in touchdown-to-interception ratio (25-6) and passer rating (101.0) and fourth in expected points added (EPA) per dropback (0.21) this season. Prescott credited his historic production to being able to play "balanced football" the last two weeks, with the Cowboys averaging the 12th-most rushing yards per game (125.5) since Week 10. "It really just opens up the whole playbook," Prescott said Thursday. "So it's a credit to all of it just, in that sense, coming together. Guys up front being physical in the run game, which then allows them to pass block a little bit easier there. And guys outside just getting open, making my job easier." In their 51-30 Week 11 win over the Titans, Schottenheimer provided Prescott and Co. their highest motion rate (63.5%) and play-action rate (58.3%) of the season, weeks after getting away from those staples through the first quarter of the year. Cowboys Pro Bowl wide receivers Lamb (1,108 receiving yards, the second most in the NFL) and George Pickens (780 receiving yards, the 11th most in the NFL) going up against the Eagles All-Pro cornerback tandem of Quinyon Mitchell and Cooper DeJean will be the key matchups on Thursday. However, Mitchell's status was uncertain because of a hamstring injury. The Eagles held walkthroughs on Monday and Tuesday, and they upgraded Mitchell to limited on Tuesday after he didn't participate on Monday. Philadelphia defensive coordinator Vic Fangio said Mitchell will be "fine" for Thanksgiving, and the Eagles listed him without a game status on the team's final injury report after he practiced fully on Wednesday, indicating he will indeed play. When the Eagles have the ball When the Eagles have the football, they'll definitely be looking to play ground-and-pound football with 2024 NFL Offensive Player of the Year running back Saquon Barkley . Barkley is currently on a streak of four consecutive games with a rushing touchdown, the longest streak of his career. The Cowboys have the worst run defense in football, allowing 151.5 rushing yards per game, and they struggle against Barkley's agile running style. Both Schottenheimer and Williams described Barkley as being a "jump cut" running back with how smoothly he can hit the hole and then glide to a different spot along the line of scrimmage and in the open field. Williams compared Barkley stylistically to Tampa Bay Buccaneers running back Bucky Irving , who went off for 165 yards and a touchdown on 21 carries in a 24-16 upset over the Cowboys in Week 5. Irving averaged a career-high 7.9 yards per carry that night at AT&T Stadium. Williams said the key is to stop Barkley's feet before he gets going. Williams also presents a challenge for Philadelphia as he leads the NFL with 18 tackles for loss, the most in a season by a defensive tackle since 2022. He also leads all defensive tackles in quarterback pressures (40) and co-leads his position in forced fumbles (4) along with Eagles defensive tackle Jalen Carter . Yet, he feels he can still find higher levels of play with the Cowboys defense allowing 20-plus points in 18 consecutive games, the longest active streak in the league. That's the longest such streak since the 2019-2021 Jacksonville Jaguars ' run of 25 straight games, per NFL Research . He completed 11 of his 21 throws for 141 passing yards while rushing for 7 yards on five carries. Prescott said he saw Milton develop most in Dallas on his mental side of the game and preparation as it pertains to pass protection adjustments and discernment at the line of scrimmage. "Joe is amazing, man. The athleticism that he has, the speed that he has, the arm talent that he has, he can do it all," Williams said. "So it's super dope to be able to go against him, especially after all the laughs and things we had in the locker room during training camp practices." The present iteration of the Eagles lacks the offensive artillery to win a duel with Prescott, Lamb and Pickens. That's especially true if Mitchell is unable to suit up on Thursday. Prescott is on a 20-game home winning streak against NFC East opponents, which is tied with Tom Brady (versus the AFC East) for the longest home winning streak by a starting quarterback against divisional opponents since the 1970 AFL/NFL merger. He'll break the tie with Brady with his 21st such victory in a row on Thanksgiving. Thursday's course will be the first Thanksgiving game in league history between two teams on winning streaks of five or more games when the NFC North rival Chicago Bears (8-2) and the Detroit Lions (8-2) square off. The league's midday entree will feature two of the biggest brands in football -- the Philadelphia and the Dallas Cowboys . A fun day of football will then be wrapped up with an AFC rivalry showdown between Patrick Mahomes ' Kansas City Chiefs and Josh Allen's Buffalo Bills . What stunning events could occur in each of the three games? Here's one bold prediction for all three courses on the Thanksgiving menu. Lions intercept Caleb Williams three times The Detroit Lions are going to intercept Chicago Bears quarterback Caleb Williams three times in Detroit on Thanksgiving. Yes, the Lions defense was a league laughingstock through the first five weeks of the season, ranking last in the NFL in both total yards allowed per game (404.4) and passing yards allowed per game (297.4). However, they have been a top-five unit in scoring defense (14.4 points per game allowed, fourth in the NFL), total defense (248.6 total yards per game, third in the NFL) and pass defense (168.6 passing yards per game allowed) since Pro Bowl defensive back Brian Branch's return from a torn Achilles after the team's Week 6 bye. In Week 11, Detroit saw All-Pro safety Kerby Joseph return from his lingering knee injury, which made Sunday the first time he and Branch have played together this season. When Branch and Joseph played in 29 of a possible 34 games together from 2023 to 2024, they combined for 20 interceptions, the most by any teammate duo in the league in that span. Their renewed partnership in the Lions secondary will lead to Williams tossing three interceptions on Thanksgiving. This game on Turkey Day will be just the second game in NFL history with both teams fresh off of at least three consecutive wins of three scores, along with Tom Brady's New England Patriots (8-0) versus Peyton Manning's Indianapolis Colts (7-0) in 2007, per CBS Sports Research. That will lead to both sides combining to score under 45 points, meaning this matchup of Mahomes vs. Allen won't be any more high-scoring than 24-20. home.headline: Eagles’ Joe Milton’s ‘revenge’ tour on Thanksgiving vs. Dallas Cowboys is a trap
home.blurb: Quarterback Joe Milton’s “return” to AT&T Stadium is not the matchup Fox and NFL people were planning on when they placed the Philadelphia Eagles against the Dallas Cowboys on Thanksgiving Day. Milton was dumped by the Cowboys after training camp, and because of Eagles’ starting quarterback Jalen Hurts being placed on injured reserve to deal with blood clots, Milton is the starting quarterback for Philadelphia. As Michigan, Tennessee, the New England Patriots and the Cowboys all know, Milton has talent. Enough talent to make some plays against a real defense, and more than enough to go big against a defense like the Dallas Cowboys. He’s also a coach killer, which is why the Cowboys are big favorites to defeat the 3-7 Eagles. The Eagles’ management has quit on the season, but as the Pittsburgh Steelers learned last week in their loss to Philadelphia, there is enough talent here to win a game. And the Cowboys have not won consecutive games since last year. The Eagles will cover, but the Cowboys will improve to .500. LogoParamountPlus More live games and exclusives Log Out Connect TV Provider More live games & exclusives Log Out Connect NFL News & Highlights Legendary quarterbacks close out the holiday slate in one of the biggest games of the season Getty Images The NFL's three-game Thanksgiving slate concludes with a blockbuster battle between two perennial playoff teams in the Buffalo Bills and Kansas City Chiefs . A pair of franchises that have regularly butted heads during the Josh Allen and Patrick Mahomes eras clash once again in one of the season's biggest showdowns to date. As is often the case when they square off in the regular season, there are significant postseason seeding implications at play in this showdown between the Bills and Chiefs. Buffalo stands in control of the AFC's No. 1 seed, while Kansas City is in a tightly contested race with the Denver Broncos for the AFC West crown and the top-four seed that comes with it. Should the Chiefs beat the Bills, not only would they solidify their standing in the division hunt, but they would also then give themselves a clear path to the top overall seed and a first-round bye. This game stands among the greatest Thanksgiving matchups in NFL history. The combined 17-3 record between the two teams is the second-best mark by win percentage entering a Thanksgiving game in the last 50 seasons. Both sides are also playing their best football of the season heading into the holiday duel. This is just the second game in league history to feature two teams riding three-game win streaks in which all of those victories came by 17 or more points. The only other such instance came in 2007 between Tom Brady's New England Patriots and Peyton Manning's Indianapolis Colts . The quarterback face-off in this contest is about as legendary as that one. Where to watch Bills vs. Chiefs live Date: Thursday, Nov. 26 | Time: 8:20 p.m. ET Location: Highmark Stadium (Orchard Park, N.Y.) TV: NBC | Streaming: Fubo ( try for free ) Follow: CBS Sports App Odds: Bills -3, O/U 50.5 via DraftKings Sportsbook Bills vs. Chiefs key storylines Another Allen vs. Mahomes classic: A pair of all-time great quarterbacks have quite the history in head-to-head battles at this stage of their careers, and there is a sharp dichotomy between their records in regular-season matchups and playoff battles. While Allen owns a commanding 5-1 lead in the regular season, Mahomes has been dominant in win-or-go-home situations at 4-0. In games against each other, their passing numbers are nearly identical; Allen passed for 1,534 yards and 11 touchdowns to Mahomes' 1,552 yards and 10 touchdowns in their first 10 clashes. Where Allen owns a decided edge is in ball security (three interceptions vs. eight) and in rushing production (five touchdowns vs. zero). Top-tier running back showdown: Messaging out of Kansas City is that the Chiefs are hopeful Kenneth Walker III will return to action on Thursday following a two-game absence due to groin tightness. If he suits up, then the NFL is in for a tremendous running back battle. Walker (109.0) and Buffalo's James Cook III (106.0) rank second and third, respectively, in rushing yards per game and are in a race with Detroit Lions star Jahmyr Gibbs for the league rushing title. If Cook can return to the top of the leaderboard, he would pace the NFL in yardage for the second consecutive year. On Sunday, he set a new record for the most consecutive games (nine) with at least 75 rushing yards and a rushing touchdown in a season. Bills defense levels up: Over the first six games of the season, the Bills had to post gaudy scoring numbers in order to make up for a leaky defense. That was not the case in any of their last four games. All of a sudden, this unit ranks 11th in EPA per play allowed, has not surrendered more than 12 points in a game since Oct. 18 and is no longer a liability but rather an asset. Defensive coordinator Jim Leonhard's unit has gone 15 quarters without allowing a touchdown, which is the NFL's longest single-season streak since 2000. The group still has to prove that it can play at this level against more formidable competition, though. Chiefs ride historic hot streak: Just like their upcoming opponent, the Chiefs enjoyed a stretch of games against lesser competition heading into the Thanksgiving battle and took care of business with ease. In routs of the New York Jets , Atlanta Falcons and Arizona Cardinals , the Chiefs tied the longest streak in franchise history of wins by at least 21 points (three). Even dating back to their last loss, Mahomes is in the midst of a scalding stretch with 13 passing touchdowns and no interceptions. Bills vs. Chiefs prediction It is difficult to knock Kansas City, because when it wins, it does so in resounding fashion and shows all the makings of a future Super Bowl winner. But the Chiefs' strength of schedule and results against projected playoff teams do raise questions about whether they can take down the Bills on the road in primetime. The Chiefs have only played three games against opponents with winning records all season and are just 1-2 in those contests. Both losses came on the road. Simply put, they have not shown an ability to win games like the one they are about to walk into. At the same time, the Bills defeated each of the three best teams on their schedule thus far. Plus, for whatever reason, Allen has Mahomes' number when they meet in the regular season. Add the defensive revival into the equation, and everything comes up Bills in this matchup. LogoParamountPlus More live games and exclusives Log Out Connect TV Provider More live games & exclusives Log Out Connect NFL News & Highlights CBS Sports writers Jordan Dajani and Jared Dubin predict this weekend's top games Getty Images Welcome to the most special week in the NFL . We watched the Los Angeles Rams defeat the Green Bay Packers on Wednesday night, and now, we have three exciting Thanksgiving matchups to digest this "Turkey Day." Football fans suffered through many sleepy Chicago Bears vs. Detroit Lions Thanksgiving matchups over the years. Now, this 1 p.m. game on Thursday is expected to be one of the most exciting holiday matchups in recent memory. After that, the Dallas Cowboys will welcome Joe Milton III and the Philadelphia Eagles to AT&T Stadium. Both teams are coming off wins, and the Cowboys need this game if they want to keep pace in the NFC East. At the end of the night, we have a potential AFC Championship preview to watch when the Buffalo Bills host Patrick Mahomes and the Kansas City Chiefs . This is just the second game in NFL history to feature two teams coming off at least three straight 17-point victories. Which teams should you pick in Week 12, and which should you fade? CBS Sports writers Jordan Dajani and Jared Dubin are here to break down the biggest games of the weekend. For clarity, lines for these selections were taken on Nov. 25 over at DraftKings Sportsbook. Credit to CBS Sports Research Chicago Bears (-1.5) at Detroit Lions (Thursday) Dajani (Bears -1.5): I can't remember being more excited for a Thanksgiving Day game, as the Bears and Lions are two of the best teams in the NFL. What I keep going back to is that the Bears are 6-0 while averaging 33.7 points in games where Caleb Williams starts and finishes. Then, factor in how much improved this Chicago defense looks with the addition of Jeffery Simmons . In Weeks 1-7, they ranked dead last in both yards per play (6.3) and yards per attempt (8.7). Over the last four weeks, the Bears now rank in the top 10 in both categories. Chicago has been swept by Detroit in each of the last two seasons. I think the Bears are done with losing to Dan Campbell … Prediction: Bears 30, Lions 28 Dubin (Lions +1.5): These are two incredibly evenly-matched teams, but it seems like Detroit has more matchup advantages offensively against Chicago's improved defense than the Bears do against the Lions' own improved unit. With Detroit also getting the benefit of home-field advantage, we're rolling with the Lions to win a close one as a home underdog. … Prediction: Lions 31, Bears 30 Philadelphia Eagles at Dallas Cowboys (-8.5) (Thursday) Dajani (Cowboys -8.5): I don't think the Cowboys have exorcised all of their defensive demons just because they blew out the Tennessee Titans , but that win at home was just what this team needed. This is one of those cases where I think the Cowboys just simply out-score their opponent. This is still a rivalry, but the Eagles are 2-8 against the spread this season, which ranks second-worst in the NFL behind the Los Angeles Chargers , and are 0-5 against the spread in their last five divisional matchups. The Cowboys should get this cover in the fourth quarter. They have scored NINETY-ONE (91) points over the past two games! That's the most in a two-game span since 1971… Prediction: Cowboys 33, Eagles 20 Dubin (Eagles +8.5): I know they just beat the Titans by 21, but I don't like laying this many points with the Cowboys. Their defense is still too suspect and they are still too prone to games where they don't perform up to expectations for me to be comfortable with an 8.5-point spread. So even while I think they'll dent the scoreboard at home on Thanksgiving afternoon, I can't bring myself to predict that this will be a blowout. … Prediction: Cowboys 30, Eagles 24 Kansas City Chiefs at Buffalo Bills (-3) (Thursday) Dajani (Chiefs +3): The craziest part about this rivalry is that the Bills have won the last five regular-season meetings, while the Chiefs have won the last four playoff meetings! You should also know that the weather is supposed to be terrible on Thursday night, so this could come down to which team runs the ball better. James Cook has recorded nine straight games with 75 rushing yards and a touchdown. He and Josh Allen are the second duo to ever account for double-digit rushing touchdowns each through the first 10 games of a season. Meanwhile, on the other side, Emmett Johnson has rushed for 206 yards with 108 receiving yards and three touchdowns over the last two games in place of the injured Kenneth Walker III . I almost think a three-point spread in this matchup is pretty high. That's going to lead me to take the points even though Bills over Chiefs has been an auto-bet in the regular season recently… Prediction: Chiefs 17, Bills 16 Dubin (Bills -3): I have basically the exact same analysis of this game as Dajani but come down on the opposite side of the bet because of the Bills' regular-season history against the Chiefs and the relative strength of their run game. I trust Josh Allen and James Cook to run the ball more than I do Emmett Johnson, even with how good Johnson has been over the last two weeks. Could Patrick Mahomes make this prediction look silly? Of course. But I think that'll prove more difficult in Thursday night's expected weather. … Prediction: Bills 21, Chiefs 17 Denver Broncos (-3.5) at Pittsburgh Steelers (Friday) Dajani ( Broncos -3.5): Aaron Rodgers lobbed a grenade into the Pittsburgh Steelers facility as he exited it this week. Going on national television and calling your coach a narcoleptic, unhealthy, lazy person who doesn't even know the franchise he works for is insane. So, this is a moment that will ultimately rally the locker room, or cause them to completely fall apart. Pick which side you'd like. The Steelers have also won and covered in six straight home games. This seems like an appropriate time for that streak to end … Prediction: Broncos 20, Steelers 13 Dubin (Broncos -3.5): After the disaster that hit the Steelers this week, I just can't see them keeping the game close against the Broncos. No, I don't think they'll get the backup quarterback bounce from Mason Rudolph . I don't trust the Broncos as far as Bo Nix or I can throw them, but given the state the Steelers' locker room has to be in right now, I think you have to roll with Denver to cover this one with relative ease. … Prediction: Broncos 24, Steelers 10 Baltimore Ravens at Houston Texans (-7) Dajani ( Ravens +7): I have the Houston Texans winning this game, but seven points seems a bit high. C.J. Stroud is playing some great football, but his production has been overshadowed by a defense that has fallen from No. 2 in points allowed per game in 2025, to 17th this year. The Texans are 1-8 against the spread in their last nine home games following an ATS win. I'll take Baltimore to keep it close… Prediction: Texans 24, Ravens 18 Dubin (Ravens +7): The Ravens have now lost six straight, but they've lost the two games in the Jacoby Brissett era by a combined five points despite turning the ball over six times in those contests. If they can just limit the giveaways, I think they might even be able to pull off an upset against a Houston team that hasn't exactly lit the world on fire this year. Either way, I think they can keep it close by throwing on a surprisingly vulnerable Texans pass defense. … Prediction: Texans 24, Ravens 20 Seattle Seahawks at San Francisco 49ers (-3) Dajani ( 49ers -3): Sam Darnold is expected to return this week, and he's accounted for 10 touchdowns compared to nine interceptions in seven starts this season. If you throw out the season opener that Drew Lock finished and won, Darnold is 2-4 as a starter this season. Believe it or not, San Francisco is 0-9 against the spread in its last nine home divisional games. With the number at a field goal, the 49ers have a good chance to end that streak this week. What they did to the Minnesota Vikings in Mexico City last Sunday night was shocking. The 49ers should be headlining everyone's NFL power rankings if they weren't already. Their 0.19 EPA per play is the best mark since the 2018 Chiefs, and they have the best offensive success rate (54.8%) by any team in a season since at least 2000 … Prediction: 49ers 24, Seahawks 20 Dubin (49ers -3): I reserve the right to flip this prediction to Seattle if Brock Purdy is out with his ankle injury, but if he's in, I just think that this San Francisco offense is a buzzsaw that can't really be stopped — even by the Dark Side defense. Remember, they dropped 32 points on Seattle the last time out. And they've scored 35 or more in each of their three games since returning from the bye. I don't think they can be stopped when everyone is healthy. … Prediction: 49ers 30, Seahawks 23 Las Vegas Raiders at Cleveland Browns (-4.5) (SNF) Dajani ( Raiders +4.5): Maybe part of me is rooting for Fernando Mendoza

That's three consecutive winning weeks for me, which is a big positive. I was 7-6 against the spread last week and 9-4 straight up. My straight-up record is now 104-58-1, while my ATS record is 75-85-3. I can see .500 now after being buried under it at the start of the season. This is Thanksgiving Week, which is usually a good week for me. And I feel good about the picks. It starts Wednesday night with a good one between the Packers and Rams , and it ends Monday night with the Bucs against the Panthers . I really like the teams in both of those games. We have NFL games Wednesday, Thursday (Thanksgiving), Friday, Sunday and Monday. What a feast. I know I will as the climb to .500 ATS continues. All lines via DraftKings ; All times ET Chicago Bears at Detroit Lions (+2.5) Thursday, 1 p.m. on CBS (Stream on Paramount+ ) This should be an offensive show. Both teams can score, even if Chicago hasn't been great on offense the past two games. On this fast track, look out. The Bears defense has played well since getting Jeffrey Simmons in a trade, but they won't stop the Lions here. Look for a lot of points with the home team getting the victory on Thanksgiving. Pick: Lions 31, Bears 27 Philadelphia Eagles at Dallas Cowboys (-8.5) Thursday, 4:30 p.m. on Fox (Stream: Fubo -- try for free) Dak Prescott has thrown nine touchdown passes and no picks in the past two weeks. The Dallas offense is rolling. The Eagles defense will be a challenge. Joe Milton, who was on the Cowboys ' practice squad, will start at quarterback for the Eagles. Dallas will play better defense against him this week. Cowboys big. Pick: Cowboys 34, Eagles 17 Kansas City Chiefs at Buffalo Bills (-3) Thursday, 8:20 p.m. on NBC (Stream: Fubo -- try for free) This is the game of the week. Patrick Mahomes vs. Josh Allen . What's not to like as two of the best in the league go at it? The Bills have played much better defense lately, but they've faced a bunch of backup quarterbacks. Not here. So look for both passers to have good days. In the end, Allen will make the big play late to win it. Pick: Bills 30, Chiefs 26 Denver Broncos at Pittsburgh Steelers (+3) Friday, 3 p.m., streaming on Amazon Prime This Friday game pits two teams who would be in the playoffs right now. But the Steelers have lost two straight and haven't looked good. Denver has won six in a row. But I think the Steelers will find a way to show up and win this one behind their running game. It won't be pretty, but the Steelers will find a way. Pick: Steelers 21, Broncos 20 New Orleans Saints at Cincinnati Bengals (-10) Sunday, 1 p.m. on CBS (Stream on Paramount+ ) The Bengals are coming off a tough road loss at Washington, while the Saints are playing consecutive road games. The Bengals offense didn't score as it had in Monday's game, but that will change here. Joe Burrow gets back on track. Bengals big. Pick: Bengals 37, Saints 20 New York Giants (-6.5) at Indianapolis Colts Sunday, 1 p.m. on Fox (Stream: Fubo -- try for free) The Giants are coming off an impressive victory over the Jaguars , while the Colts are coming off a bye. They released quarterback Daniel Jones , which means Anthony Richardson will be starting. The Giants' defense should dominate in this one. The Colts have packed it in, so the Giants take it. Pick: Giants 27, Colts 10 New York Jets at Miami Dolphins (+3.5) The Jets are playing consecutive road games, while the Dolphins are home for the first time in three weeks. The Jets played well in beating the Chargers last week, while Miami lost to the Bills. The Dolphins are limited on offense, but the Jets' defense has struggled. Look for Miami to hang around. Pick: Jets 23, Dolphins 21 Atlanta Falcons at Minnesota Vikings (-7) The Vikings are home after getting blown out by the 49ers in Mexico. The Falcons are off a bye. The Minnesota offense struggled against the 49ers, but the Falcons have had defensive problems lately. Look for the Minnesota defense to get back on track as well. Vikings take it. Pick: Vikings 28, Falcons 14 Tennessee Titans at Jacksonville Jaguars (-14.5) The Jaguars are coming off a bad showing in the loss to the Giants, while Tennessee gave up 51 to the Cowboys last week. Ouch. The Jaguars scored 40 against them two weeks ago. They won't get that many here, but it will still be ugly as Trevor Lawrence and the passing game get back on track. Pick: Jaguars 33, Titans 13 Baltimore Ravens at Houston Texans (-7) This is essentially a playoff game of sorts for these two. The loser is pretty much done. The Texans are home off a Thursday game, while the Ravens are playing consecutive road games. Edge Houston. The Texans have played well on offense, and the Ravens' defense is a mess. Look for a big day for C.J. Stroud . Pick: Texans 31, Ravens 23 New England Patriots at Los Angeles Chargers (-1.5) Sunday, 4:05 p.m. on CBS (Stream on Paramount+ ) This was once scheduled for prime time, but it was moved because both teams have flopped this year. The Patriots will start Tommy DeVito for the injured Drake Maye . That's a problem. The Chargers might not have Justin Herbert (concussion) either, which would put D.J. Uiagalelei in as the starter. He's thrown seven passes in his career. Even so, give me the home team here. Pick: Chargers 23, Patriots 16 Washington Commanders (-7) at Arizona Cardinals Sunday, 4:25 p.m. on Fox (Stream: Fubo -- try for free) The Commanders are coming off an impressive home victory Monday night over the Bengals, while the Cardinals got rocked by the Chiefs last week. Arizona has big-time issues and fired the defensive coordinator this week. That defense will struggle to stop Jayden Daniels . The Commanders stay hot. Pick: Commanders 30, Cardinals 19 Seattle Seahawks at San Francisco 49ers (-3.5) The 49ers have the best record in the NFC and seem to be cruising to the division title. But Seattle can slow that talk down here with a victory. That will be tough to do on the road. Look for a lower-scoring game in the second division game between the two — the 49ers won the first — and San Francisco will win it late. Pick: 49ers 21, Seahawks 17 Las Vegas Raiders at Cleveland Browns (-4.5) Sunday, 8:20 p.m. on NBC (Stream: Fubo -- try for free) This has been flexed to prime time because the Browns would be a playoff team right now. Plus, the Raiders have rookie Fernando Mendoza making his third start. The Raiders are playing consecutive road games, and Cleveland is off a bye. Big edge to the Browns as they win it behind their defense. Pick: Browns 27, Raiders 19 Carolina Panthers at Tampa Bay Buccaneers (-3) Monday, 8:15 p.m. on ESPN, ABC (Stream: Fubo -- try for free) The Panthers can take a stronghold on the division with a victory here. They come in with defensive issues, but the Bucs have problems in the passing game. So what gives? I think the Tampa Bay defense will play well here and the Bucs will run it right at Carolina to win it like they did in the first meeting. Pick: Bucs 23, Panthers 17 Green Bay Packers (+2.5) at Los Angeles Rams Wednesday, 8 p.m., streaming on Netflix The Packers get Micah Parsons back, while the Rams will be without Puka Nacua for the rest of the season. Their offense is limited without him. But this game will be decided by how well the Packers' line can block Aaron Donald and Myles Garrett . They've been bad, but I think they will be better here. The defense will keep this close, and Jordan Love will win it late. For the first time in either team's history, they will meet on Thanksgiving Day when Buffalo hosts Kansas City at Highmark Stadium. Last year, Andy Reid's squad fell to the Cowboys on Thanksgiving two weeks before Patrick Mahomes went down with a torn ACL and LCL . Kansas City is hoping for a better result this time around as it battles with the Bills for the top seed in the AFC. Fans have circled this matchup on their calendars since the schedule came out. Mahomes and Josh Allen have produced some instant classics over the years, though Mahomes has prevailed when it mattered most. The Bills are looking to finally get over the hump against KC. Heading into this marquee showdown, what does the ESPN Matchup Predictor forecast? Here's what the computer model projects two days before kickoff. Chiefs on SI's Take It's hard to argue that the Chiefs aren't favored over a one-loss team on its home field. Buffalo's only loss came in an outlier performance against the Patriots, who have since lost Drake Maye and may miss the postseason. They boast a 9-1 record with strong wins over the Lions, Rams, and Texans. The issue with the Bills has not been in regular-season matchups against KC. Allen currently holds an all-time 5-1 record over Mahomes in the regular season — the Chiefs seemingly become Allen's kryptonite in the playoffs, where Buffalo has lost all four contests during his tenure. Buffalo's defense has had a massive impact on its recent winning streak, as it has not allowed a touchdown for 15 consecutive quarters. It has faced a few terrible offenses during that stretch, but it is still an impressive feat to watch out for nonetheless. The Chiefs are optimistic they will get Kenneth Walker back this week, which makes things interesting given the emergence of rookie running back Emmett Johnson . They could form a dangerous two-headed monster against this strong Bills defensive unit. Regardless of who is favored by oddsmakers, it should be a memorable matchup between two of the top contenders in the AFC. While the Bills have played in 11 games on Thanksgiving Day , this is the first time they will be at home for the holiday. The game itself will be full of intrigue as two of the top teams in the AFC will square off in a game that will have huge implications on the AFC playoffs seeding. Both teams come in on a winning streak, but the Bills' recent wins haven't inspired much confidence. Buffalo has faced multiple backup quarterbacks, and while they did what good teams should do and won each time, they apparently didn't win convincingly enough.
